notes: Round 6, two Scanner shapes where bash runs the command and the checker is silent, both in the header's accepted pass-through class and not shapes a maintainer writes (notes, not failures): (a) `2>&1 bun install` — a redirection with an fd digit written before the command word leaves the digit as the command (`bun install 2>&1`, the ordinary order, is named); a one-line fix drops an all-digit word that immediately precedes `<`/`>`; the header's claim that `2>&1` is never a word holds only after the command. (b) a comment inside backticks runs to the newline rather than the closing tick, swallowing what follows the tick on that line (already named in the implementer's trickyParts).
Round 6: the Scanner names `bun install` inside a heredoc body (bash does not run it) — a conservative false positive no real workflow reaches.

Round 5 correction to round 4's record: round 4's two backslash probes (`bun \` + `install`; a continued argument line) were mis-built — Python's string continuation had already joined their lines before the YAML was written, so they exercised one-line commands, not the join. This round's probes pass the text raw; the real continuation is joined and named, the comment-backslash and escaped-backslash shapes are not joined, and the continued argument line is allowed.
Round 5: no residual gap found in the tokeniser's comment/continuation handling among the seven shapes probed.

Round 4: no residual gap found. A mode-only change to the manifest (executable bit) alongside the exact bump would pass the content rule (`git diff --name-only` lists the file; the JSON is equal) — harmless (a file mode on package.json) and not reproduced here since `jq > tmp && mv` rewrites the mode; noted for completeness.

Round 3: no residual checker gap found among the probes; the header's documented pass-through class is now `xargs`/`nohup` and a variable in command position. The one false-positive class (a `shell:` first word other than bash/sh, e.g. `/bin/bash`, and `npm` with a leading flag) is conservative and absent from the real workflows.

A bash killed by SIGTERM mid-push (a cancelled job) does not run its EXIT trap, so the deploy-key directory would outlive the command on the runner's disk until the ephemeral runner is destroyed; the spec covers exit paths, not signals, and GitHub-hosted runners are ephemeral — noted for completeness.

`npm --version` and `npm` with a leading flag (`npm --registry … publish`) are refused in a credentialed job (conservative false positive); the real publish jobs spell `npm view` and `npm publish` plainly and pass.

The merge will cut a listener release: at main b5761883 and the head, `release-push.sh version legion-envoy-v …` gives 13.4.1 (6aeee579d's fix(dispatch) touched packages/envoy after legion-envoy-v13.4.0), so the first merge-triggered release-envoy-listener.yaml run is a release-cutting run (release_build stamps 13.4.1, release_publish confirms with --expect, tags, attests, releases) — the production check can record the listener's full path on that run, and `imagetools create` without setup-buildx-action is exercised there.

Hardening, not pinned: `no-credential`'s `find ~/.ssh -mindepth 1` does not descend when `~/.ssh` is a symlink to a directory (prints the listing, reports clean) and `[ -d ~/.ssh ]` reports a regular file as `absent`; both are sandbox-evasion shapes outside the tripwire's stated remit (`find -L` or a trailing slash closes the first). `Actions/Checkout@<sha>` (mis-cased owner/repo) in a build job skips rule 3 (`startswith('actions/checkout@')`); whether GitHub resolves that casing was not provable from this pod (the review App cannot write workflows to legion-smoke), so it is a note. `docker run <image>` in a credentialed job passes the checker (only `docker build`/`buildx build` are denied). `${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` or any `secrets.*` beyond GITHUB_TOKEN in a build job is not read as a credential; the red case covers only the DEPLOY_KEY index form.

Environment: PyYAML (a uv venv), jq 1.7 and openssh-client 10.0 were installed under $HOME/.local for the local runs; the pod image has none of them (the implement handoff recorded the same for its container). The `jq` builtin of the harness shell is jaq; the scripts ran under bash with the real jq first on PATH.

Tests not re-run: lint, typecheck and the unit suites are CI's (cited above); `go version -m` on a cross-built agent-secrets binary and `agent-secrets --version` were not re-measured here (planner's measurement in plan.json specDepartures; first executed on the merge-triggered listener run).
